body:
**Tier:** not assigned (C suggested; same class as #908). Split from #908 via PR #1027.

PR #1027 moves the **L2-country** read gate out of the build fingerprint (`Country._read_l2_country_cache`, in `_build_registry._EXCLUDED_CALLABLES`), so a logic edit to it no longer cold-rebuilds the corpus. The **wave-tier** read gates are still fingerprinted mechanism, i.e. a logic edit to them still moves every table's hash:

- the `cache_freshness` call inside `Wave.grab_data` (`country.py` ~:1558 at review time);
- the `cache_freshness` call inside `run_make_target` (~:1862);
- the `assume_cache_fresh` serve (~:4358).

**Remaining work:** extract these the same way, check behaviour is identical branch by branch, and pin with a no-op-edit probe like #1027's `test_editing_the_read_gate_moves_no_hash` (with a positive control). The extraction itself invalidates the corpus once, so it should be bundled with another re-warm.

Evidence: red-team verdict on PR #1027 §5.4 (backlog sweep 2026-10-17).

comments.body: Fixed on `development` by PR #1105, the corpus bundle (merge `e87a551e8`). Left open until the release merge to `master`.

title: Wave-tier cache read gates are still inside the build fingerprint (Wave.grab_data, run_make_target, assume_cache_fresh serve)
